paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: Probing accuracy with reduced training data.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the probing accuracy of two multilingual BERT models—mBERT and XLM-R—across varying training data sizes. The x-axis, labeled "Train size," represents the number of training examples, ranging from 200 to 2000 in increments of 250, with a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," measures the model's performance, scaled from 80 to 94 in increments of 2, also on a linear scale. The legend indicates that the light blue line with 'x' markers corresponds to the mBERT model, while the dark blue line with 'x' markers represents the XLM-R model. Both models show an increasing trend in accuracy as the training size grows. The mBERT model starts at an accuracy of approximately 83.0 when the training size is 200 and steadily increases to about 90.2 at a training size of 2000. The XLM-R model begins at a higher accuracy of around 84.8 and rises to approximately 91.8 at the largest training size. Throughout the entire range of training sizes, the XLM-R model consistently achieves higher accuracy than the mBERT model.
